features.summary: Firefox now checks video codec support more carefully, including H.264 and HEVC hardware and software decoding, color depth, and frame size, so reported capabilities better match what a device can actually play. The changes also improve FFmpeg’s MediaCodec encoding controls and HEVC format handling, and make Vulkan Video decoding more reliable across Linux drivers.

features.summary: Firefox now waits for the GPU process and compositor’s video bridge to be ready before creating remote video decoders and encoders. Sharing the right texture information across processes should make video playback more resilient when those components restart; added logging helps diagnose their lifetimes.

features.summary: Video decoders for media elements now use the current image bridge, helping them stay connected to the right display pipeline. The accompanying cleanup makes media metadata events and DOMMediaStream listeners easier to manage, with no major new user-facing feature.

features.summary: When a tab permanently loses audio focus, Firefox now stops treating its audio as active; a temporary loss still keeps the tab gated. This better distinguishes a lasting handoff from a brief interruption, and the related tests now wait until audio sessions are actually active.

features.summary: WebCodecs VideoFrame handling now preserves the original coded frame dimensions even when the visible image is cropped, and tests verify that geometry. It also avoids repeating internal format conversions, helping keep frame processing consistent and efficient.

features.summary: When a content decryption module (CDM), which handles DRM-protected media, terminates, Firefox now notifies MediaKeys before shutting down its connection to that module. This gives encrypted playback a clearer termination sequence; the other change is formatting-tool compatibility with no user-visible effect.

features.summary: Media Capabilities now reports power efficiency more accurately for HEVC and codecs without a specified profile, helping websites choose suitable video playback options. Firefox also avoids shutting down while a strict decoder check is waiting or underway, so these capability queries can finish reliably.
